candidate.answerReason: One man's daily rate is f/(bc), so c men lay f/b bricks per day. They need b/(f/b)=b^2/f days to lay b bricks.

methods.label: Find one worker's rate
methods.explanation:
Finding one man's daily rate lets us use the same productivity for the new crew. Since \(b\) men lay \(f\) bricks in \(c\) days, one man lays
\[
\frac{f}{bc}
\]
bricks per day. Therefore \(c\) men lay
\[
c\cdot\frac{f}{bc}=\frac{f}{b}
\]
bricks per day.

Let \(d\) be the number of days this crew needs to lay \(b\) bricks. Work equals daily rate times time, so
\[
\frac{f}{b}d=b,
\qquad
 d=\frac{b}{f/b}=\frac{b^2}{f}.
\]
The quantities \(b,c,f\) are positive in this work situation, so all divisions are valid. The answer is \(\boxed{\dfrac{b^2}{f}}\) days, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: A unit work rate and elementary algebraic division suffice.
